comparison.basis: the last published build dated before this one

categories.label: New published records
categories.meaning: Records found by research and reviewed before publication. The dates shown are when the events happened, not when they were found: a record dated before the previous build is the record catching up, not a new disruption.

categories.label: Records withdrawn or held on review
categories.meaning: Records the previous build showed and this one does not: withdrawn, or held while a review is repeated. The record changed, not the world.

categories.label: Research coverage changed
categories.meaning: A research pass was logged, the state of a search changed, or published records were re-reviewed. This describes the search, not events.

categories.label: Source link health re-checked
categories.meaning: Cited pages or registry sources were visited again. A re-check says something about the sources, not about any event.

categories.label: Methodology or rule change
categories.meaning: How records are admitted, placed, published or scored changed. A rule change can move what is shown with nothing changing in the world; it never means a country improved or worsened.

categories.label: Data correction
categories.meaning: A published record's date, place, class, figure, wording or sources were corrected, or a reference input was edited.

categories.label: National context updated
categories.meaning: National energy statistics were refreshed. Context only: never a disruption record, never part of an index.

categories.label: Recovery evidence added (where publishable)
categories.meaning: A report about recovery was added to an existing record. It may describe a restoration long before this build. Facility status under an active attack campaign is never shown here.

categories.label: Index moved by time decay only
categories.meaning: No input changed. The evaluation date moved and modelled impairment aged. This is not evidence that anything was repaired.

categories.label: Build-only change
categories.meaning: The site was rebuilt. No published record, rule or context changed.

order: systems alphabetically by name; never by size, count or severity
note: What changed in the published data, by cause. Dates on records are when the events happened. No counts are shown: reporting differs too much between countries for a number beside each to mean anything but a ranking.

notes: A reference source snapshot or the source register was refreshed.
